book.meridian_story.xunxi.note: The swordplay of Chen Ke, a lone swordsman. He never strikes first; he answers once the other blade has run its course.
volume.meridian_story.xunxi_full.note: At your foster father’s grave, Chen Ke knew an old friend’s swordwork and taught this volume himself, only as far as true qi.
codex.source.meridian_story.xunxi_full: The gravekeeper broke Chen Ke’s guard at your foster father’s grave and was taught there; forms beyond reach wait for a later visit.
codex.power.meridian_story.xunxi_full: Sidestep needs only your legs and is open to mortals. Delayed Thrust and Retreating Lift need true qi and one open hand meridian.
technique.meridian_story.side_step.note: Step aside to the left or right, out of a blade coming straight on. The step itself harms no one.
technique.meridian_story.held_thrust.not: Fix on one foe and where they stand, hold, then thrust straight. If they have moved, the point finds air.
technique.meridian_story.back_lift.note: Step back, then cut upward at the foe in front. With no room behind you, the cut never comes.
volume.meridian_story.yunxi_lower.note: Two indigo ties hold the lower scroll beside the upper one in the gravekeeper’s pack.
codex.source.meridian_story.yunxi_lower: Two indigo ties hold the lower scroll beside the upper one in the gravekeeper’s pack.
codex.power.meridian_story.yunxi_lower: Open two hand meridians and one foot meridian. Channel true qi through your sword to strike with Cloud Cleaver, Shadow Return and Twin Pearls.
story.meridian_story.fate.pay.hint: Pay eight coppers to hear what you carry.
story.meridian_story.fate.pay.after: The coppers ring and he weighs the bowl. “You were born with a baleful current. Deserters pick a fight. Beasts follow it over a ridge. Walk shoulder to shoulder with someone and they'll take the first blow. Opening a meridian takes you longer than most. Yet corner you, and you've still got a blow left in you. Both come of the same thing.”
story.meridian_story.fate.leave.hint: Keep your coppers and leave the rest unheard.
story.meridian_story.fate.leave.after: A few steps on, you hear him murmur, “That current goes where you go…” The scrape of his poker swallows the rest.
story.meridian_story.fate.accompany: Walk with him to the village
story.meridian_story.fate.accompany.hint: Look after him as far as the gate. Beside you, he'll draw danger too.
story.meridian_story.fate.accompany.afte: At your nod he catches up, shifting the awkward banner to his outside shoulder to leave you half the path.
story.meridian_story.fate.dismiss: Send him away at the fork
story.meridian_story.fate.dismiss.hint: Part here. He keeps the banner and its cord.
story.meridian_story.fate.dismiss.after: You block his way and point down the other fork. He starts to speak, then settles for “Take care.” The cord is still tied to the banner.
story.meridian_story.fate.search: Search the deserter for the slip
story.meridian_story.fate.search.hint: Take this slip and see who offered payment.
story.meridian_story.fate.search.after: You unfold the slip. “Draw out the baleful current when the bearer strikes back. Bring a wisp to the torn-banner temple for payment.” Beside his mark the writer added, “For my practice.” A sketch on the back shows the broken banner and the path.
story.meridian_story.fate.mark.hint: Leave the slip here to collect later.
story.meridian_story.fate.mark.after: You take a good look at the roadside stone. That corner of yellow paper is still showing.
story.meridian_story.fate.drawn: Draw the current in and accept your fate
story.meridian_story.fate.drawn.hint: Keep the current within you. Cornered, you strike harder and longer. Trouble comes more often, and would-be companions draw back. This is a lasting choice.
story.meridian_story.fate.drawn.after: Following the folded page, you draw the cold at your wrist back in. Your fingers close slowly. The strength stays there even after you open your hand.
story.meridian_story.fate.stilled: Still the current and break with your fate
story.meridian_story.fate.stilled.hint: Let the current ebb. Fewer troubles will find you, and others can walk beside you. Your last-ditch counter will be weaker. This is a lasting choice.
story.meridian_story.fate.stilled.after: You follow the line on the page until the cold across your hand begins to lift. When you make a fist, a little of the strength that once held you up is gone. You try again, learning the feel of it.
story.meridian_story.fate.later.hint: Keep the notebook. Either path can wait.
story.meridian_story.fate.later.after: You run a thumb along the crease, close the notebook, and tuck it away.
story.meridian_story.fate.reading: As you turn onto the village road, a man is warming his hands under a tree. The fire dips when you draw near. The blind fortune-teller turns an ear to your footsteps and tucks his hands back into his sleeves. “Hard luck for your kin. Whoever walks close to you bleeds.” He feels for the rim of his bowl and nudges it toward you. “Want the rest?”
story.meridian_story.fate.escort.scene: You meet a young escort on the mountain road with an old banner rolled under his arm. He tightens a loose knot at its tail. “I'm headed for that village gate too. Narrow road. We can take turns in front.” You tell him he'd do better to keep clear. He shoulders the banner. “I heard you. Shall we go?”
story.meridian_story.fate.temple: At the end of the temple passage, a man wipes a ring of ash from the lip of a clay jar. “I paid them to bring me a wisp. And here you are in person.” He sets down the lid and stays squarely between you and the temple door. None of the men on the road ever stood their ground like that.
story.meridian_story.fate.strike.after: The bowl strikes the ground at your feet. A copper rolls into the grass. You heard him quite clearly when he said that those close to you would bleed.
story.meridian_story.fate.death.after: The banner lies at his feet. You tighten the loose knot just as he did, then tighten it again. When you look up, you're still leaving him half the road.
story.meridian_story.fate.gate.blood: At the gate he unties the cord from his old banner and presses it into your hand. “Walk with you and there's blood all along the road. That's true enough.” He pats your shoulder. “But you turned back.”
story.meridian_story.fate.ambush: The banner pole cracks against the ground. Your assailant has slipped past your shoulder. Behind you the escort shouts, “Turn round! It's me they're after!”
story.meridian_story.fate.gate.safe: He unties the cord. “I heard them coming past you. Good thing you turned back.”
story.meridian_story.fate.gate.quiet: At the gate he stops. “That’s my home ahead. You kept looking back for me all this way.”
story.meridian_story.fate.hired: A corner of yellow paper shows inside his collar, with “bounty” scrawled across it. The paper stirs in the wind. In all your travels, this is the first bounty slip you’ve seen on one of them.
story.meridian_story.fate.poor: You feel through your pockets. There aren’t eight coppers there.
story.meridian_story.fate.follow: Follow the directions on the slip
story.meridian_story.fate.follow.hint: Mark the temple and make the journey yourself.
story.meridian_story.fate.follow.after: You commit the torn banner to memory.
story.meridian_story.fate.arrival: You find stoppered clay jars under the torn banner. As you step into the side passage, someone taps a fingernail lightly against the shoulder of a jar.
story.meridian_story.fate.return: When you return to the torn banner, the jar is still there. Inside, the man puts its lid back. “You again?”
story.meridian_story.fate.retreat.hint: Leave the temple and return another day.
story.meridian_story.fate.retreat.after: You remember the tapping of his fingernail on clay.
story.meridian_story.fate.victory: He falls beside the altar, a worn notebook open by his hand. The familiar cold is still in your chest.
story.meridian_story.fate.take.hint: Keep the notebook. Read it in hand before deciding.
story.meridian_story.fate.take.after: You tuck the worn notebook away.
story.meridian_story.fate.read.after: You turn to a folded corner. “Draw it in, and its strength is yours in danger. Let it gather, and trouble comes. Still it and let it disperse, and the road is kinder to your companions. Your strength thins with it.” Someone traced that last line twice.
story.meridian_story.fate.direction: About %s paces %s, under the torn banner.
story.meridian_story.fate.recover.hint: Recover your own missing evidence here.
story.meridian_story.fate.no_site: You cannot yet make out the place on the slip. Try again later.
story.meridian_story.fate.fear: The traveler draws level with you, then shifts the pack back to the other shoulder. “You go ahead. I could use a rest.”
story.meridian_story.fate.together: The traveler moves the pack aside to make room.
letter.meridian_story.lone_star_fate.sli: The exact torn-banner temple location: %s, %s, %s. Use in hand to inspect.
letter.meridian_story.lone_star_fate.not: One page is dog-eared. Use in hand to read.
letter.meridian_story.lone_star_fate.cor: The cord the young escort untied at the village gate.
technique.meridian_story.cloud_cleaver.n: Cut diagonally from above at a single foe. A parry brings your blade partway into the cut.
technique.meridian_story.shadow_return.n: Twist to sweep your sword at someone behind you, then snap back. Keep facing forward.
technique.meridian_story.twin_pearls.not: Strike twice in a row at someone in front of you. If they step back, the second strike misses.
technique.meridian_story.flash_parry.not: Raise your blade across your brow. Catch the incoming blow and draw back into a diagonal cut.
story.meridian_story.road.walk: On the road alone, you remember the waybill in a stray soldier’s collar. Look for one when someone bars your way.
story.meridian_story.road.lodge: Charcoal smudges the corner of the waybill. Warm your hands at a campfire and speak to the porter there.
story.meridian_story.road.scene: The footman spots the waybill in your hand and shifts aside to make room for you by the fire.
story.meridian_story.road.waybill_receiv: The footman takes the waybill from your hand.
story.meridian_story.road.greeting: Rough road tonight. Walk with me a while? If you’d sooner go alone, I have a road token.
story.meridian_story.road.escort: Hand over the waybill and escort him
story.meridian_story.road.solo: Hand over the waybill and take the token alone
story.meridian_story.road.escort_reply: Keep the stub. If they catch us, listen for my call. I know a way through.
story.meridian_story.road.solo_reply: Take this token. If they come after you, show it to me for a way out.
story.meridian_story.road.night_escort: Pocket the stub, open your first meridian, then head out. Survive the night; when pursuers arrive, the footman will point the way—fight or slip clear.
story.meridian_story.road.night_solo: Open your first meridian, take the road token, and head out to survive the night. If pursuers find you, ask the footman to switch routes or break free on your own.
story.meridian_story.road.guide: Quick, down this path beside me!
story.meridian_story.road.exchange: Hand over the road token and slip down the side path
story.meridian_story.road.return_escort: The escort is done, dust thick on your boots. Gripping the stub, you return to the fire to claim your rations from the footman.
story.meridian_story.road.return_solo: You outrun the pursuers and hurry back to the campfire, breathing hard. You pull out the receipt for the footman to inspect.
story.meridian_story.road.give_food: Hand over the stub and claim the rations
story.meridian_story.road.give_pass: Present the receipt and claim the pass
story.meridian_story.road.end_escort: Thanks for seeing me through. Here, a loaf for the road.
story.meridian_story.road.end_solo: There’s your stamp. Take care at the forks ahead.
story.meridian_story.road.camp: The firelight warms your hands. You claim this camp.
Frayed edges, flecked with dried mud.
letter.meridian_story.lone_star.escort_s: Show this to the footman by the fire for rations.
letter.meridian_story.lone_star.road_tok: Bring to the footman to switch routes when pursued.
letter.meridian_story.lone_star.safe_stu: A guiding receipt given after the footman takes your token.
letter.meridian_story.lone_star.loaf.lor: Hearty wheat scent, in thanks for the escort.
letter.meridian_story.lone_star.pass.lor: Crisp seal. Carry this for the roads ahead.
story.meridian_story.road.follow: Follow the porter down the side path
book.meridian_story.yunxi.note: Your foster father left two volumes. The first relies on arm strength, the second on true qi.
volume.meridian_story.yunxi_upper.note: Indigo cord binds the upper scroll your foster father left in the gravekeeper’s pack.
technique.meridian_story.wind_thrust.not: The point shoots straight ahead. A step to the side lets it pass.
technique.meridian_story.moon_lift.note: The point lifts in a short arc, catching two foes standing shoulder to shoulder.
technique.meridian_story.yunxi_sword_req: Take a sword in hand first.
codex.source.meridian_story.yunxi_upper: Indigo cord binds the upper scroll your foster father left in the gravekeeper’s pack.
codex.power.meridian_story.yunxi_upper: Thrust at a distant foe, sweep at two standing close, or raise the blade across your brow to parry.
story.meridian_story.reborn.roll: Name in the old ledger. Someone asks after you along the road. When they arrive, check where their leader falls.
story.meridian_story.reborn.seal: Reversed seal. You spot your past life's death date on the torn page. That ferry seal broke long ago—why is this mark still backward? Ask a villager to compare seals, or keep the paper and wait for the next crew's counter-seal.
story.meridian_story.reborn.alone: You tuck the torn page close. Watch the road, wait for the next leader to show, and seize their counter-seal to compare.
story.meridian_story.reborn.ledger: Name added after death. You press the two seal marks together. Ask someone by the village bell to check the old register; if no village is nearby, wait for the next crew carrying a ledger copy.
story.meridian_story.reborn.sign: Altered signature. After your death, someone claimed your stored goods under your name. Hand the testimony to a witness, or wait for the next wave and seize the forged seal.
story.meridian_story.reborn.hand: Hand over page to match seals
story.meridian_story.reborn.compare_repl: This seal is backward. Take it.
story.meridian_story.reborn.archive_repl: It's in the register. Keep this testimony safe.
story.meridian_story.reborn.carry_reply: If you're taking it, hold onto this page yourself.
story.meridian_story.reborn.publish_repl: I'll correct the old record for you, and put in a good word.
letter.meridian_story.reborn.fragment.lo: Frayed paper edges. Black ink clearly marks the death date of your past life.
A backward mark pressed into the paper. Left by the broken old seal from the ferry.
letter.meridian_story.reborn.testimony.l: Dry ink on testimony. States someone used your name to claim stored goods after you died.
letter.meridian_story.reborn.private_let: Stamped with the forged seal. The old case is clear, yet your foes will still come.
letter.meridian_story.reborn.public_lett: Only the forged signature is corrected here. Record set straight, yet your foes will come again.
origin.meridian_story.ordinary.name: Ordinary Upbringing
origin.meridian_story.ordinary.story: You grew up in an ordinary family down the street, often tending the stove as a child.
origin.meridian_story.lone_star.story: Growing up with courier caravans, you faced trouble even at inn doors. Years on the road made you tougher than most.
origin.meridian_story.lone_star.talent.1: Sprinting, leaping, or swinging—you outlast others at the same work.
origin.meridian_story.lone_star.talent.2: Even badly hurt, you can grit your teeth and force out a few quick strikes. Once that surge fades, you must recover before doing it again.
origin.meridian_story.lone_star.threat.1: When opening your meridians, you must hold that breath a little longer than others.
origin.meridian_story.lone_star.threat.2: You were born with a baleful current. Trouble finds you on the road, and whoever walks beside you may bleed.
origin.meridian_story.lone_star.name: Lone Star
effect.meridian_story.gritted_counter.no: Though badly hurt, a surge of strength in your arms lets you strike faster for a while.
story.meridian_story.reborn.seal_greetin: Will you let me see the seal on the torn page?
story.meridian_story.reborn.ledger_greet: What will you do with the signed page in the old ledger?
story.meridian_story.reborn.sign_greetin: Will you leave your testimony to set this old case right?
chat.meridian_story.replaced: You put away the replacement paper.
chat.meridian_story.later: You take your leave for now. You can come back another day.
chat.meridian_story.defer: Leave for now and return another day
story.meridian_story.reborn.seal_scene: A villager holds out an open palm before you, waiting to see the seal.
story.meridian_story.reborn.ledger_scene: By the village bell, a villager opens an old ledger before you, not writing yet.
story.meridian_story.reborn.sign_scene: You step up to the witness. He stops what he's doing, waiting for you to speak.
origin.meridian_story.grave_keeper.name: Sword Tomb Keeper
origin.meridian_story.grave_keeper.story: Adopted and raised by a swordsman in your youth. After his passing, you carry his old sword and watch over his grave.
origin.meridian_story.grave_keeper.talen: You wear your foster father’s old sword. His notes, both volumes of the Yunxi Sword Manual and a guide to his grave lie in your pack.
origin.meridian_story.grave_keeper.threa: Stay away from your adoptive father too long, and your mind grows restless.
Old acquaintances will trace the past and seek you out at the tomb.
effect.meridian_story.homesick.note: You haven't visited the grave in too long; your heart can't seem to settle.
item.meridian_story.grave_marker.lore: Moss covers a corner of the low headstone, its stone surface cold to the touch.
item.meridian_story.grave_sword.lore: The indigo cloth wrapped around the hilt has faded to gray, yet it still feels steady in your hand.
item.meridian_story.grave_guide.lore: Follow the vermilion line on the paper; at its end lies your adoptive father's grave.
item.meridian_story.yunxi_notes.lore: Old papers left behind by your adoptive father, with a tea stain on the corner of a page.
story.meridian_story.tomb.directions: You follow the vermilion line on the paper to find the tomb: Overworld (%s, %s, %s).
story.meridian_story.tomb.wait: The ink on the guide hasn't settled; the sword tomb's location remains unknown.
story.meridian_story.tomb.swept: You brush the moss from the headstone and sit quietly before your adoptive father for a while.
story.meridian_story.tomb.sad: You haven't visited your adoptive father in days, and your mind keeps wandering.
book.meridian_story.yunxi_notes.page: That year, just as the autumn rain stopped, he came to my house clutching an old sword to ask for wine. I remember a sliver of moonlight flashing beneath the hem of his robe, followed a breath later by two crisp chimes close together under the veranda. Only after the second sound settled did he finally drop his stiff airs. He leaned his sword by the door, warmed his hands by the hearth, and even complained that the tea I brewed was too weak—when he was the one who had promised to bring the wine.
story.meridian_story.friend.name: Senior Zhou
story.meridian_story.friend.scene: Footsteps stop behind you. Your father's old friend holds a bunch of wildflowers.
story.meridian_story.friend.greeting: You're the child who always watched him wipe his sword, aren't you? How fast you've grown. I picked some wildflowers. May I set them by his stone?
story.meridian_story.friend.welcome: Take the wildflowers and set them by the stone
story.meridian_story.friend.refuse: Ask him to take the wildflowers away
story.meridian_story.friend.thanks: Thank you. After cleaning his sword he used to sit on the porch and look at these flowers.
story.meridian_story.friend.hurt: Very well. I'll take them with me.
story.meridian_story.rival.name: Chen Ke
story.meridian_story.rival.scene: You return to the sword mound and see a middle-aged man standing at the edge of the clearing, holding a straight sword and looking at the main stele.
story.meridian_story.rival.greeting: Used to squat on the threshold watching him wipe his blade, rubbing your thumb just like that. All grown now.
story.meridian_story.rival.invite: He could break my stance back then. Come, try it with the sword he left you.
story.meridian_story.rival.accept_hint: Hold a sword and step into the clearing. He only defends.
story.meridian_story.rival.decline: Only here to tend the grave today
story.meridian_story.rival.unlearned: Your father wrote down what happened the day I came knocking. Check his old notes again.
story.meridian_story.rival.unarmed: Take your sword in hand first.
story.meridian_story.rival.outside: Step into the clearing and stand steady.
story.meridian_story.rival.busy: You look over; his sword is already set in a guard.
story.meridian_story.rival.stand: Only after you stand steady does Chen Ke bring his sword across his chest.
story.meridian_story.rival.declined: He nods to you, says no more of sparring, tells you he will come another day, and turns to leave.
story.meridian_story.rival.recognized: Thought the first was luck. Then those next two rings—hah, it's your father again.
story.meridian_story.rival.interrupted: I'm here to see an old friend's kid. Another day.
story.meridian_story.rival.teach_offer: Keep your father's book safe. Mine's the Xunxi Sword Manual, and it only goes as far as true qi. Want to learn?
story.meridian_story.rival.teach_accept_: Learn the Xunxi Sword Manual from him. Forms you can take now are learned on the spot; the rest wait for next time.
story.meridian_story.rival.teach_defer_h: Pass for now. He will come back to teach when you next return to the mound.
story.meridian_story.rival.taught: You follow him through the forms once, then sheathe your sword.
story.meridian_story.rival.teach_done: That's all of it. If your father could see this, he'd nod. I'm off.
story.meridian_story.rival.teach_pending: The last two need true qi, and your hand meridians aren't clear yet. Practice this step first. I'll come back when you're through.
story.meridian_story.rival.teach_deferre: All right. The manual isn't going anywhere. I'll teach you next time.
story.meridian_story.rival.resume_scene: You return to the sword mound. Chen Ke is already standing at the edge of the clearing, looking up toward you.
story.meridian_story.rival.resume: You're here. We didn't finish last time. Let's pick it back up.
item.meridian_story.grave_fragment.lore: A broken edge Zhou kept for your father.
story.meridian_story.tomb.repaired: You smooth the notch out of the blade.
story.meridian_story.tomb.reforge_cost: Uses one iron ingot and one fragment. The previous sword loses its mark.
story.meridian_story.fallen.opening: You hear someone breathing in the grass by the bend. A cultivator lies curled in the mud, his coat torn and one corner of his scroll dark with blood. When you crouch, he can still pull it closer to his chest. A loose stone rattles beyond the bend. Then it goes quiet.
story.meridian_story.fallen.rescue: Dress his wound and give him medicine
story.meridian_story.fallen.rescue.cost: This will take one Potion of Healing. Anyone on his trail may come after you too.
story.meridian_story.fallen.leave.cost: Leave him here with his belongings.
story.meridian_story.fallen.rescue.good: He opens his eyes and looks from you to the scroll under his palm. “Take the clean end.” This time he holds it out to you.
story.meridian_story.fallen.rescue.bad: You have just tied the bandage when a shout comes from the bend. “Stop the one helping him, too!” The wounded man uses your arm to get to his feet.
story.meridian_story.fallen.escort.safe: The footsteps fade. He leans on you until he can speak and points back to the fork. “That's where they came up.”
story.meridian_story.fallen.escort.lost: When you look back, he's gone. A scrap of the bandage you tied catches in the grass.
story.meridian_story.fallen.escort.died: You lift your head from his side. The hand that held your sleeve has gone slack.
story.meridian_story.fallen.wrest.good: The scroll comes free in your hand. You look back along the bend. The road is empty.
story.meridian_story.fallen.wrest.bad: You pull the scroll free and rub the cover with your thumb. Beneath the drying blood, half a red seal and the name of his school are still legible.
story.meridian_story.fallen.wrest.missed: You step back to the roadside. The bloodstained scroll is still held against his chest.
story.meridian_story.fallen.school: Someone at the crossroads holds up a red seal. “You recognize this from the cover, don't you?”
story.meridian_story.fallen.leave.done: You walk on around the bend. For a few steps you can still hear him breathing. Then all you hear is the scuff of your own boots.
story.meridian_story.fallen.gone: You return to the spot where you met. They're gone.
story.meridian_story.seller.opening: As you pass a roadside table, the seller gives the scroll on it yet another dusting with his sleeve. The edges are frayed and the ink smells damp. “Try ten markets. You won't see another like it.” He nudges it half an inch toward you, keeping his other hand on the cover.
story.meridian_story.seller.buy.good: Once you've paid, you brush off the cover and trace the ink from the first stroke to the last. Every movement leads into the next. This is a form you can actually practise.
story.meridian_story.seller.buy.bad: You pay and open the book. One diagram runs off the edge. The next page repeats it exactly, right down to the same stray blot.
story.meridian_story.seller.practice.don: You follow the broken line for one breath and it catches wrong. You brace yourself until the strength comes back to your legs.
story.meridian_story.seller.close.done: You roll the book shut. The line of wet ink leaves a smudge inside its cover.
story.meridian_story.seller.wreck.good: Half-written scraps roll out from under the table. The seller bolts, too frightened to turn back even for the purse that falls from his belt.
story.meridian_story.seller.wreck.bad: That night you hear the day's sales cry again, this time behind you. An answering call comes from the dark, then footsteps from both directions.
story.meridian_story.seller.leave.done: You walk around the table. Each price he calls after you is lower than the last.
story.meridian_story.frantic.opening: A basket lies on its side at the village entrance. You see a red-eyed cultivator lashing out at anyone in reach, blood showing at his cuff. A fellow disciple calls his name again and again. He never turns. There are still villagers at the mouth of the lane. The last one bends to shift the basket out of the way.
story.meridian_story.frantic.hold.good: After a while he recognizes the faces around him. When you let go, he takes something from his coat. “Please take it. I'm sorry. Did I hit anyone?”
story.meridian_story.frantic.hold.bad: You feel his arm go slack. Then he twists out from under yours and runs straight for the lane.
story.meridian_story.frantic.injured: You hear a cry from the lane. By the time you get there, the disciple has caught the villager who was struck and is asking where it hurts.
story.meridian_story.frantic.safe: You hold him long enough for the last villager to make the lane. The disciple takes over and you let go of the dusty sleeve.
story.meridian_story.frantic.kill.good: The cultivator lies still. The villager who moved the basket comes back to you, his voice unsteady. “Thank you. I was next.”
story.meridian_story.frantic.kill.bad: The disciple kneels by the body and calls to his senior one last time. Then he looks up at you. “He didn't know anyone just then. I'll know your face.”
story.meridian_story.frantic.feed.good: The salve still smells bitter on your fingers. At last he hears the disciple calling him. The man helps him sit, frees one hand, and bows to you.
story.meridian_story.frantic.feed.bad: He has barely swallowed the salve when he pushes the disciple away. At the mouth of the lane you hear the villagers backing up again.
story.meridian_story.seller.buy.cost: The book costs %s if you buy it. The seller won’t stand behind what’s written inside.
story.meridian_story.seller.unavailable: The money and goods cannot change hands yet.
story.meridian_story.seller.wreck: [Attack] Wreck the stall and seize the seller
story.meridian_story.seller.leave.cost: Leave with your money and leave him the book.
story.meridian_story.seller.practice: Try the form in the book
story.meridian_story.seller.practice.cos: The diagram breaks off halfway. Forcing the next breath may leave you weak.
story.meridian_story.seller.close.cost: Put the book away and leave the exercise alone.
story.meridian_story.frantic.hold: [Attack] Bring him down and hold your next blow
story.meridian_story.frantic.feed: Give the disciple Bitter Yellow Paste for him
story.meridian_story.frantic.cost: Spend one dose of Bitter Yellow Paste on his wounds. It may still take more to calm him.
story.meridian_story.followup.win: You wait on the road until the last of them has drawn away. No one looks back.
story.meridian_story.followup.escape: You stop and listen. This time the footsteps behind you are just your own echo.
story.meridian_story.followup.loss: By the time you can stand steadily again, they've gone.
story.meridian_story.debt.opening: You round a bend and find a youth in the middle of the road, a worn blade hanging by his leg. He gives a name you remember. “%s. You killed him. He was my father.” He switches the blade to wipe his palm on his coat, then takes it back. There's room to pass, but he won't step aside.
story.meridian_story.debt.pay.cost: Pay him %s. The money will be his, whether or not he forgives you.
story.meridian_story.debt.truth: Tell him his father struck first
story.meridian_story.debt.truth.cost: Give your account of the fight. He'll hear it once.
story.meridian_story.debt.paid_good: The youth weighs the silver and sheathes his blade at last. “My mother's waiting for me.” This time he steps aside.
story.meridian_story.debt.paid_bad: The youth ties the silver up tight. “I'm taking this because we need it at home. When I know how to use this blade, I'll come back.” You watch him follow the road away.
story.meridian_story.debt.youth_return: You recognize the old blade. This time the hand holding it is steady. “I told you I'd be back.”
story.meridian_story.debt.killed: The youth lies in the road, the worn blade beside his hand. You wait a moment. He makes no sound.
story.meridian_story.debt.spared: You step back so he can get up on his own. He retrieves the old blade. A few paces down the road he says, “Next time my hand will be steady.”
story.meridian_story.debt.separated: A stretch of road opens between you. You both stop fighting, out of breath. He's still on his feet with his blade in hand.
story.meridian_story.debt.youth_master: A stranger gives the youth's name and asks twice if you knew him. Only when you answer does he unstrap his blade. “He was my student.”
story.meridian_story.debt.truth_good: You tell it from the start. He studies you for a while, lowers his blade, and steps out of your way without a word.
story.meridian_story.debt.truth_bad: His grip tightens on the hilt. “You lived. You get to say whatever you like.” He stays in the road.
story.meridian_story.herb.opening: You follow a bitter scent up the cliff. A pair of wither roses is coming into bloom, black petals peeling back from the calyx. A wolf below the ledge lifts its head. Across the slope a gatherer sets down a basket and shows you the end of a rope. Someone farther down the road has stopped to look up as well.
story.meridian_story.herb.solo: Drive off the wolf and climb first for the roses
story.meridian_story.herb.share: Gather the roses together and take one each
story.meridian_story.herb.share.cost: Split the pair. While you pick, the stranger will be at your back.
story.meridian_story.herb.inquire: Ask what the buyer will pay for the way up
story.meridian_story.herb.inquire.cost: Name the trail only after payment. The buyer gets the harvest.
story.meridian_story.herb.solo_good: You slide down the back of the ledge with both roses in hand. The wolf is still staring up at the empty cleft.
story.meridian_story.herb.herb_ambush: You have just put away both blooms when someone steps across the path down. He eyes your coat. “Saves me the climb.”
story.meridian_story.herb.shared_good: The rope draws tight and you come over the ledge. When you split the pair, the gatherer leaves you the longer-stemmed rose.
story.meridian_story.herb.shared_bad: You have a rose apiece when the rope goes slack behind you. The hand that pulled you up is reaching for your flower.
story.meridian_story.herb.sold_good: Only when the silver is in your hand do you point out the cleft. The buyer takes the narrow path uphill.
story.meridian_story.herb.sold_bad: You put the silver away, but the buyer doesn't climb. He steps into the middle of your path. “Who else knows the way up?”
story.meridian_story.herb.lost: Back at the foot of the cliff, you open your hand. A little black pollen sticks to your palm.
story.meridian_story.debt.name: The avenging youth
story.meridian_story.herb.agreed: The gatherer sets down the basket and waits for you to pick the roses.
story.meridian_story.herb.quote: The buyer weighs his purse. “I’ll pay %s for that trail.”
story.meridian_story.herb.sell.cost: Take %s and give the buyer the trail to this plant.
story.meridian_story.herb.poor: The buyer feels his purse and makes no offer.
story.meridian_story.herb.space: Make room in your pack for the trail map.
story.meridian_story.herb.returning: You hold the roses close and turn down the trail.
story.meridian_story.herb.won: The man falls on the trail. Your way is clear.
story.meridian_story.debt.youth_retry: The youth steps into your path once more, worn blade in hand.
story.meridian_story.debt.gone: You return to the spot where you met. They're gone.
story.meridian_story.herb.gone: You return to the spot where you met. They're gone.
story.meridian_story.mountain.win: You wait on the road until the last of them has drawn away. No one looks back.
story.meridian_story.mountain.escape: You stop and listen. This time the footsteps behind you are just your own echo.
story.meridian_story.mountain.loss: By the time you can stand steadily again, they've gone.
story.meridian_story.youth_return.name: The returning youth
story.meridian_story.youth_retry.name: The avenging youth
story.meridian_story.youth_master.name: The youth’s master
story.meridian_story.herb_ambush.name: Trail robber
story.meridian_story.escort_cart.opening: You round the bend and find the convoy banner in the mud. Two guards lie dead behind it. The others stand with their backs to the wagon shafts, a crate between them. A man coming down the bank knocks his hilt against the wagon. “Just passing? Take the high ground.” His eyes stay on the captain.
story.meridian_story.escort_cart.paid: The bandits pull back. The captain unties a silver ingot from his belt and gives it to you. “Remember our banner. Next time you see us, walk with the wagon a while.”
story.meridian_story.escort_cart.claimed: The claimant presses an old bill against the crate. You can see the maker’s mark matches the one on the bill, right down to a chip in its rim. “Who guarded this load?”
story.meridian_story.escort_cart.returne: You turn the crate until the chipped mark lines up with the one on the bill. Its owner folds up the paper and wheels the crate away himself.
story.meridian_story.escort_cart.favor: You recognize the crooked banner. A guard makes room by the wagon. “Remember? Walk with us. I'll tell you when we reach the fork.”
story.meridian_story.escort_cart.share: The guards give way. A bandit eases a crate off the shafts and holds it with his shoulder until you have it. “Your share, like we said.”
story.meridian_story.escort_cart.wanted: A bounty notice flaps by the road. You stop. The likeness is poor, but you can read the charge beneath it. Wanted for helping rob a convoy.
story.meridian_story.escort_cart.convoy_: You see your likeness again. This time it's in a guard's hand. He checks it against your face and folds it away. “That's you.”
story.meridian_story.escort_cart.salvage: Both parties limp away with their wounded. You come down the bank. A crate is still beside the fallen banner, its rope severed.
story.meridian_story.escort_cart.spotted: The road goes quiet. The victors step over the fallen banner and look straight up at you. “There's one more on the bank.”
story.meridian_story.escort_cart.withdra: You leave the mountain road. A wagon board thumps behind you. Nobody calls you back for a share.
story.meridian_story.escort_cart.watch: Wait out the fight on the bank
story.meridian_story.escort_cart.watch.c: Stay for the length of the fight. They can see you from the road.
story.meridian_story.escort_cart.return: Return the crate to its owner
Give back the crate bearing the matching mark: %s
story.meridian_story.escort_cart.fork: Here is the fork. Safe travels.
story.meridian_story.village_ring.openin: When the gong falls silent, you hear coins hitting the bottom of a wooden box. Below the platform the bookmaker rolls up his sleeves. A fighter knots a white strip around his wrist. A silver purse hangs from the corner post beside the steps. The ringmaster taps the post. “Hold the ring for three bouts and I'll cut it down for you.”
story.meridian_story.village_ring.won: The crowd gives you three cheers. You still have a hand on the corner post as the ringmaster cuts the red cord and drops the purse into your palm.
story.meridian_story.village_ring.hurt: The bookmaker doesn't even look up when the third fighter climbs in. You leave the ring hurt. When you look back, the man has taken his place behind the bookmaker again.
story.meridian_story.village_ring.left: You step down. The planks creak behind you. The purse is still on its post.
story.meridian_story.village_ring.bet_go: The white sash goes up. The bookmaker counts your stake back onto the table, then counts out the same amount again.
story.meridian_story.village_ring.bet_ba: You catch the bookmaker twitch the corner of his mouth. The man in the white sash still has both feet planted when he bows and yields. The bookmaker sweeps your stake into the box.
story.meridian_story.village_ring.expose: The false lots scatter from beneath the table. Once the bettors have their stakes back, one catches up with you and presses a few coppers into your hand.
story.meridian_story.village_ring.pursui: The men behind the table leave their stools and chase you beyond the village with clubs. You hear one of them panting. “Get those hands that tipped the table!”
story.meridian_story.village_ring.enter: Step into the ring for three bouts
Win all three for the purse. You can step down between bouts.
story.meridian_story.village_ring.bet: Back the fighter in the white sash
story.meridian_story.village_ring.bet.co: Stake %s. Win and take back your stake plus as much again. Lose and the house keeps it.
story.meridian_story.village_ring.lots: False lots from under the table
story.meridian_story.village_ring.ring_e: The hired hands catch up, clubs in hand.
story.meridian_story.convoy_warrant.name: Warrant officer
story.meridian_story.ring_enforcers.name: Hired enforcer
story.meridian_story.midnight.opening: At midnight you pass the ruined temple. Two white lanterns hang below the steps where you saw none before. One lights a spread of old goods, the other a row of sealed silver parcels. You can see the wares clearly, but not the traders’ faces. As you step closer, the buyer turns a parcel to show its seal. “I'll take your goods if you can wait till dawn to open this.”
story.meridian_story.midnight.bought: Once you've paid, a hand reaches into the light and gives you the relic you picked. Only when you put it away does the low murmur of trading resume behind you.
story.meridian_story.midnight.scratching: You reach into your coat and touch what you bought at the market. Something scratches behind you. When you take two steps left, the scratching follows.
story.meridian_story.midnight.sold: You set the goods down and the trader passes the sealed parcel across. You turn it over. The price on the seal is the one you agreed.
story.meridian_story.midnight.silver: At dawn you tear along the seal and count out the silver. Every bit of the night's unlikely price is there.
story.meridian_story.midnight.paper: At dawn you break the seal. The pieces inside are shaped like silver ingots. The moment you rub one between your fingers, it folds like the paper it is.
story.meridian_story.midnight.strike: The instant you strike, both lanterns go out. You stand before the empty steps. One last voice in the dark speaks to you. “We'll take no more of your business here.”
story.meridian_story.midnight.dawn: You watch the eastern sky grow pale. Bamboo poles knock together as the lanterns come down. The steps bear no trace of either stall.
story.meridian_story.midnight.replacemen: You take the replacement parcel. The old seal is void.
story.meridian_story.midnight.reissue.co: Void the old seal and claim a replacement on the original terms.
story.meridian_story.midnight.buy.cost: %s, priced at %s. Nobody here will tell you who owned it.
story.meridian_story.midnight.sell.cost: Give %s for a parcel marked %s qian of silver. It opens at dawn, and nobody vouches for the silver inside.
story.meridian_story.midnight.open.cost: Break the seal on this payment and take what is inside.
story.meridian_story.midnight.unavailabl: The money, goods or space for the exchange are missing.
story.meridian_story.bequest.opening: Bitter herbs scent the cave. You follow the drip of water to an old man sitting against a stone bed with a jade pendant held to his chest. He raises it to the lamp to show you the worn cord hole. “My disciple is waiting at the village gate. Will you take this there for me? I can't take what strength I have left with me.”
story.meridian_story.bequest.accepted: Heat travels from his palm past the place where your own flow always stopped. He winds the cord around your hand. “Don’t leave him waiting.”
story.meridian_story.bequest.marked: You open your hand and he settles the cord in your palm. You draw a breath of essence and feel it pass the place where it used to stop.
story.meridian_story.bequest.overdue: The day you promised has passed. You wonder how often the disciple has gone out to the gate to look for you. It's hard to get on with what you were doing.
story.meridian_story.bequest.delivered: The disciple takes the jade, his thumb finding the worn cord hole. “He kept it.” You had half a journey to work out what to say. Now you don't need to.
story.meridian_story.bequest.bequest_ene: The stranger bars your way. “Let me see that current again. I want to know if he taught you.”
story.meridian_story.bequest.notes_given: The old man lets out a breath and draws no more. As you straighten his coat, a folded note slips out. On the back, a single form is drawn from first movement to last.
story.meridian_story.bequest.notes_left: The elder on the stone bed is still. A note lies beside him, a damp thumbprint just beneath the signature.
story.meridian_story.bequest.accuse: The disciple bends over the stone bed, one hand on the note. He looks back at you. “That day, was there anyone in here besides you and my master?”
story.meridian_story.bequest.looted: The slipknot comes loose in your hand. The old man reaches out, but you already have the bundle.
story.meridian_story.bequest.struck: Just as you grip the bundle, his palm catches you in the chest. You back against the rock empty-handed. It takes a while to draw a full breath.
story.meridian_story.bequest.elder: The elder by the stone bed
story.meridian_story.bequest.accept.cost: Deliver the jade to the village gate at %s within five online days. You can still deliver it later.
story.meridian_story.bequest.decline.cos: Leave the jade and the errand with him.
story.meridian_story.bequest.attack: You can also strike and take the bundle.
story.meridian_story.bequest.deliver: Give the jade to the disciple
story.meridian_story.bequest.deliver.cos: Hand over this jade and fulfil your promise.
story.meridian_story.bequest.replace.cos: Invalidate the lost jade and issue a replacement.
story.meridian_story.bequest.replaced: At the stone table you thread the replacement cord.
story.meridian_story.bequest.study.cost: Practice the sidestep on the reverse, subject to its learning requirements.
story.meridian_story.bequest.unready: You cannot yet perform the form drawn on the reverse.
story.meridian_story.bequest.learned: You fold the note and retrace the steps.
story.meridian_story.bequest.gone: When you return, the stone bed is empty.
story.meridian_story.bequest.bequest_acc: A stranger answers the disciple’s call and bars your way.
story.meridian_story.bequest_enemy.name: The elder’s enemy
